Code review feedback identified API design violations, formatting bugs, register size mismatches, and animation timing regressions.

Changes validated via build verification. Visual behavior matches original implementation (parallel fade-out). Register display now shows correct bit widths.

## Summary
Consolidated FAQ implementations across multiple pages by extracting inline FAQ data and rendering logic into a reusable `FAQSection` component. This refactoring centralizes FAQ content in a dedicated data file while reducing code duplication and improving maintainability.

## Key Changes

- **Created centralized FAQ data file** (`src/data/faqs.ts`): Moved all FAQ content from individual page files into organized, named exports for each page (e.g., `tenancyAgreementTemplateFAQs`, `eicrFAQs`, `evictionNoticeTemplateFAQs`, etc.)

- **Replaced inline FAQ rendering**: Updated 15+ pages to use the `FAQSection` component from `@/components/seo/FAQSection` instead of inline map/render logic

- **Removed redundant structured data**: Eliminated inline `faqPageSchema` generation from individual pages, as the `FAQSection` component handles schema generation internally

- **Updated imports**: Changed FAQ component imports from `@/components/marketing/FAQSection` to `@/components/seo/FAQSection` for consistency

- **Standardized FAQ section styling**: All FAQ sections now use consistent props (`faqs`, `title`, `showContactCTA`, `variant`) for uniform appearance and behavior

## Pages Updated
- Assured Shorthold Tenancy Agreement Template
- EICR Landlord Requirements
- Eviction Notice Template
- Eviction Notice UK
- Form 3 Section 8
- Form 6A Section 21
- How to Evict Tenant
- How to Rent Guide
- Lodger Agreement Template
- MCOL Money Claim Online
- And 7+ additional pages

## Benefits
- **DRY principle**: Single source of truth for FAQ content
- **Easier maintenance**: Update FAQ content in one place
- **Consistent UX**: Standardized FAQ rendering across all pages
- **Reduced bundle size**: Eliminated duplicate FAQ rendering logic
- **Better SEO**: Centralized schema generation ensures consistency

Implemented the "Blocked Content" feature. This allows users to mark specific articles (by URL/Title) as blocked from the frontend UI. These blocked items are saved to a new Google Sheet named `blocked_content`. The scraper now loads this list and filters out any blocked URLs or Titles from future search results. author: djoregenese
body:
## Problem

The containers page crashes with `attempt to index field '?' (a nil value)` when a container references an image that has neither `RepoTags` nor `RepoDigests`.

This commonly occurs with:
- Intermediate build layers from failed/interrupted `docker build` runs
- Locally built images that haven't been tagged
- Orphaned containers referencing deleted images

## Root Cause

Line 88 in `containers.lua` calls `next(iv.RepoDigests)` without first checking if `iv.RepoDigests` is `nil`. In Lua, `next(nil)` throws an error, while `next({})` safely returns `nil`.

```lua
-- Before (crashes when iv.RepoDigests is nil):
data[index]["_image"] = iv.RepoTags and iv.RepoTags[1] or (next(iv.RepoDigests) and ...

-- After (handles all nil cases):
data[index]["_image"] = (iv.RepoTags and iv.RepoTags[1]) or (iv.RepoDigests and next(iv.RepoDigests) and ...) or "<none>:<none>"
```

## Fix

Add a nil check for `iv.RepoDigests` before calling `next()`, and use `<none>:<none>` as the fallback value to match Docker's standard display format for untagged images.

## Testing

Tested on OpenWrt with Docker 27.3.1. Before the fix, the containers page would crash when any container referenced an image with no tags or digests. After the fix, such containers display correctly with `<none>:<none>` as the image name.

Fixes #197

author: miewest
body:
## Problem

`Stapler.getCurrentRequest()` returns null when code runs outside an HTTP request context (e.g., MultiBranch Pipeline indexing, SCM polling, or pipeline execution on an executor). The existing code assumed it could always fall back to the Stapler request context, but didn't null-check before calling `findAncestorObject()`.

This caused NPEs like:
```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke
"org.kohsuke.stapler.StaplerRequest.findAncestorObject(java.lang.Class)"
because the return value of "org.kohsuke.stapler.Stapler.getCurrentRequest()" is null
  at org.conjur.jenkins.api.ConjurAPI.getSecretFromConjurWithInheritance(ConjurAPI.java:642)
```

The bug was introduced in v3.0.0 (2025-05-23) with the "inheritance for Secrets and Configuration" feature, which added `getSecretFromConjurWithInheritance()`. This method tries to walk up the folder hierarchy to find valid Conjur config, and assumed it would always have either:
- A valid `context` passed in, OR
- A valid Stapler request to derive context from

Neither is true when called from background job execution.

## Call chain example (MultiBranch Pipeline)
```
Executor.run() 
  → WorkflowRun.run()
    → SCMBinder.create()
      → SCMSource.fetch()
        → GitHubSCMSource.retrieve()
          → Connector.connect()  [needs GitHub credentials]
            → ConjurSecretUsernameCredentialsImpl.getPassword()
              → ConjurAPI.getSecretFromConjurWithInheritance()
                → Stapler.getCurrentRequest()  ← returns null!
```

## Fix

Check if `getCurrentRequest()` returns null before trying to use it. If both context and currentRequest are null, fall back to `Jenkins.get()` (which was already in the code path, just not reachable).

Applied the same null-check pattern to 4 locations:
1. `ConjurAPI.java` - `getSecretFromConjurWithInheritance()`
2. `ConjurAPIUtils.java` - `getItemFromReferer()`
3. `ConjurCredentialStore.java` - `hasPermission2()`
4. `ConjurCredentialStore.java` - `getCredentials()`

## Testing

- All 344 existing tests pass
- Added regression test to verify fix remains in place
- Tested with `mvn clean verify` on Java 17

## Related Issues

This may help resolve or partially address:
- Possibly related to #42 (folder config issues after upgrade)
- Possibly related to #40 (pipelines failing after upgrade to v3.0.x)

## Description The existing test_1to1_with_ros2sub already covered: Agnocast Pub -> Agnocast Sub (Native) Agnocast Pub -> ROS 2 Sub (Bridge A2R) This PR adds the missing direction: ROS 2 Pub -> Agnocast Sub (Bridge R2A). (Note: ROS 2 -> ROS 2 communication is included.) Key Changes - Implemented a test node using pure rclcpp::Publisher. - Introduced the use_agnocast_pub flag to toggle between Agnocast native publisher and standard ROS 2 publisher, enabling full bidirectional coverage. - Documented the behavioral difference between A2R (Exit Burst) and R2A (Entry Burst & Replay) in the test code. - Changed the shutdown condition for both TestSubscriber and TestTakeSubscriber from "receiving N messages" to "receiving a message with ID >= Target End ID". This change makes the test robust against DDS burst behavior (Transient Local), where duplicates or dropped messages in the Bridge buffer could previously cause premature termination or hanging. ### Subsucriber Test Expectations Summary The expected message count and verification behavior vary by the combination of Publisher, Subscriber, and QoS settings: | Publisher Type | Subscriber Type | Pub QoS | Sub QoS | Expected Behavior | Verification Logic | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Agnocast** | **Agnocast**

(Exact match for all history & live) | | **Agnocast** | **ROS 2** | `Transient Local` | `Transient Local` | **Burst History + Live** | **Fuzzy (History) + Strict (Live)**

author: shuoranliu
body:
When accessing files from UFS (e.g., S3, OSS) via FUSE mount, the access() system call was failing with EACCES (errno 13), even though ls -l showed correct permissions (0777).

Root cause:
- FileStatus returned by UFS layers used `..Default::default()` which set mode to 0 (u32::default())
- In FUSE's status_to_attr(), there was a fallback: when mode == 0, use FUSE_DEFAULT_MODE (0o777). This made ls -l display correct perms.
- However, check_access_permissions() used raw status.mode directly without this fallback, causing permission checks to fail.

Example log before fix:
  Access check: mode=0, permission_bits=0, mask=4 Read permission check: requested=true, granted=false FuseError { errno: 13, error: "Permission denied" }

Fix:
- Add explicit `mode: 0o777` in FileStatus construction for:
  - opendal.rs: write_status(), read_status()
  - oss_hdfs_filesystem.rs: new_file_status()

Note: file_status_from_info() in oss_hdfs already reads actual permissions from JindoFileInfo, so no change needed there.

## Root Cause
HTTP Basic Auth is applied at infrastructure layer:
- Web server (nginx/Apache) Basic Auth on dev.arcane.city subdomain, OR
- Shield package environment-based activation via `SHIELD_USER`/`SHIELD_PASSWORD` env vars

## Changes

**Documentation**
- Added `SHIELD_PROTECTION_ISSUE.md` with investigation results and fix instructions for deployment team
- Updated `.env.example` with warnings that Shield env vars may trigger global auth
- Added clarifying comments to `config/shield.php`

**API Routes** (unrelated to web route issue)
- Moved events/entities/series/tags endpoints out of `auth.either` middleware to public group
- Applied `auth:sanctum` only to write operations (POST/PUT/DELETE)
- Fixed route ordering (specific routes before parameterized)

## Fix Location
Not in application code. Requires infrastructure changes:

```bash
# Option 1: Remove nginx Basic Auth
auth_basic off;  # in server block for dev.arcane.city

# Option 2: Clear Shield env vars
SHIELD_USER=
SHIELD_PASSWORD=
```

author: guest0x0
body:
Consider a task spawned with `allow_failure=false` (the default). If the task is cancelled, should it be considered failing (and hence fail the whole task group)? Previously, such cancelled task is considered non-failing only if the cancellation come from the task group itself (i.e. the task group is already performing cleanup). Tasks manually cancelled via `Task::cancel` are considered failing. This semantic is inconsistent and surprising (if users want to manually cancel task, they must pass `allow_failure=true` to `@async.spawn`).

This PR refines the semantic by *not* treating cancelled task as failing unconditionally in task groups. This should simplify the semantic and improve user experience for manual task cancellation. Note that if the task raise another error during cancellation handling, it is still treated as failing.

body:
## Summary
Implemented a custom hover animation for call-to-action buttons that transforms a pill-shaped button into a square with a coordinated icon swipe effect. This replaces the previous SVG background approach with a more dynamic, interactive animation using GSAP.

## Key Changes

- **New Button Hover Module** (`scripts/btn-hover.js`)
  - Created dedicated animation module with configurable parameters (swipe distance, duration, easing)
  - Implements pill-to-square morphing with circular icon exit and square icon entrance
  - Includes proper cleanup function for page transitions to prevent memory leaks
  - Fully documented with inline comments explaining animation logic

- **Updated Button Markup & Styling** (`styles.css`)
  - Replaced SVG background image with clean, semantic HTML structure
  - Button now contains text wrapper and two icon elements (circle and square)
  - Simplified styling: white background, orange icons, 56px height
  - Added GPU acceleration with `will-change` property for smooth animations

- **Integrated with Page Transition System** (`scripts/barba.js`)
  - Added `initBtnHover()` call to initialize animations on page load
  - Added `destroyBtnHover()` cleanup before page transitions
  - Ensures proper resource management during Barba.js navigation

- **Updated Link Hover Module** (`scripts/link-hover.js`)
  - Excluded `.btn` elements from generic link hover animation
  - Removed button-specific flexbox handling since buttons now use dedicated animation
  - Simplified code by removing conditional logic for button styling

- **Updated Button Text** (`index.html`)
  - Changed CTA text from "LOREM IPSUM" to "Let's Start Investing"

## Implementation Details

The animation uses a staggered timeline approach:
- Container border-radius morphs from 50px (pill) to 4px (square) over 0.5s
- Circle icon translates right and fades out while square icon translates left and fades in
- Slight stagger (0.05s) between icon animations creates a swipe effect
- All animations use `power2.inOut` easing for premium feel
- Configuration object allows easy tweaking of animation parameters without code changes
